checks.name: Works named
checks.meaning: Distinct codes. A code is a work: a tablet, a prayer within one, an excerpt that circulates on its own.

checks.name: Texts held
checks.meaning: Rows — one work in one language, from one source.

checks.name: Languages
checks.meaning: Counting every language in which we hold at least one text.

checks.name: Books catalogued
checks.meaning: Collections with a known item order.

groups.title: Findability
groups.note: A work nobody can search for is, in practice, unnamed. This is the measure that matters most, and the one hardest to move.

checks.name: Works in one language only
checks.meaning: Usually an original with no translation yet. Not an error — no language is guaranteed to exist for any work — but it is the ceiling on who can read it.

checks.name: Works in no widely-read language
checks.meaning: Reachable only by someone who reads the original.

checks.name: Works given an English first line
checks.meaning: Works holding no English text at all, for which the catalogue's own English opening is surfaced in search — so the work can be found and identified even where no translation exists. Counted over whole works only: attaching a tablet's opening to an excerpt of it would misstate what the excerpt is. Overlaps the row above without being a subset of it.

groups.title: Identity
groups.note: Every text must carry a name. A missing name is the one state the catalogue does not allow.

checks.name: Texts with no code
checks.meaning: Must be zero. A text with no name cannot gather its translations.

checks.name: Identity pending (TMP)
checks.meaning: One work, identity not yet established. Constitutive but deferred — an honest state, not a defect.

checks.name: Identity absent (X)
checks.meaning: Identity could not be established with the tools used. Reopened whenever better tools arrive.

checks.name: Malformed codes
checks.meaning: Codes that do not parse. Should be zero.

groups.title: Integrity
groups.note: Every reference should resolve. These are the checks that catch a rename that swept some tables but not all.

checks.name: Orphaned prayer-book entries
checks.meaning: Structure rows pointing at a code that holds no text.

checks.name: Texts that are empty
checks.meaning: A row that names a work but holds no text for it, so it gathers nothing and gives a reader nothing.

checks.name: Texts with leaked markup
checks.meaning: Scraper residue, not markup as such. Stored HTML is normal here — 34,000 rows carry paragraph tags that render through Markdown — so this looks only for a stray <div wrapper or double-escaped markup, neither of which belongs in a text.

groups.title: Linguistic signals
groups.note: These are proxies, not proofs. Each correlates with a real class of error, each has honest exceptions, and none should be acted on without reading the rows. They exist because a corpus this size in this many languages cannot be checked by reading it.

checks.name: Texts not in their language's script
checks.meaning: A row labelled Persian written in Latin letters, or the reverse. Usually a mislabelled language or a transliteration filed as the original. Only languages with an unambiguous script are tested, and only when one script dominates the text.

checks.name: One code and language, two unrelated texts
checks.meaning: The same work claimed twice in one language by texts that share almost no words. Holding several renderings of a prayer in a language is normal and not counted here — a second translation still carries the same names and epithets. Texts under forty words are also left out, because at that length a rubric like to be recited at noon outweighs the prayer itself.

checks.name: One item labelled as two languages
checks.meaning: Byte-identical text carrying two different language labels, so one of them is wrong — invisible to a script test when the languages share an alphabet, as with Polish filed as Vietnamese or Slovak as Swedish. Most of the current count is a single fault: 61 paragraphs of the Words of Paradise whose Spanish, French and Portuguese rows hold the English text verbatim, so a reader asking for Spanish is served English. Persian/Arabic pairs are excluded by design — there the label records which section of the source a row came from — as are variant labels of one language, which are two editions rather than a mislabelling.

checks.name: One text under two different works
checks.meaning: Identical text filed under two codes. Sometimes a genuine duplicate from two sources, sometimes a work that has been split in two by mistake. Worth reading either way.
